identification.summary: Microsoft describes Storm-1249 as a China-based espionage actor that typically uses generic phishing lures to target high-level officials at organizations of interest [S1]. Storm-1249 is a Microsoft 'Storm' designation, i.e. a group still in development [S2].
identification.notes: Only one public Microsoft passage found; it appears in the device code phishing section of the post, but the text does not say Storm-1249 uses device code flow [S1]. A secondary blog reportedly lists Storm-1249 among device code phishing groups; this could not be opened and is unverified. Do not merge with Storm-2372, which Microsoft discusses separately in the same post [S1].

attribution.basis: Microsoft labels the actor 'China-based' and 'espionage' [S1]. No government attribution, named sponsoring organization, or Microsoft confidence statement was found.

targeting.notes: Microsoft says the actor targets high-level officials at organizations of interest; no sectors or regions are specified [S1].

capabilities.summary: Microsoft states Storm-1249 typically uses generic phishing lures on topics such as taxes, civil service, and book pre-orders [S1]. The post does not state a specific technique, malware, or infrastructure for this actor [S1].

campaigns.name: Microsoft public mention (identity attack techniques post)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's 2025-05-29 post names Storm-1249 as a China-based espionage actor using generic phishing lures against high-level officials [S1]. No discrete campaign, victim, or date of activity is given.

diamond.adversary: China-based espionage actor per Microsoft; unnamed in other vendor taxonomies [S1].
diamond.capability: Phishing with generic lures (taxes, civil service, book pre-orders) [S1].
diamond.victim: High-level officials at organizations of interest [S1].

gaps: No dedicated Microsoft report on Storm-1249 found; only one passage in the 2025-05-29 post.
Whether Storm-1249 uses device code phishing is not confirmed by Microsoft's text [S1]; secondary-blog claim (admindroid) could not be fetched.
Sectors, regions, malware, infrastructure, first-observed date, and any overlap with named China-based clusters are unknown.
Searches for the bare designation returned no other relevant reporting.
No government attribution or confidence assessment found.
